answers.answer: When the key expires, concurrent misses can each read the same schedule and overload the 500-read/second database. Coalesce them: keep one lookup in progress and let concurrent readers share its result, avoiding one database read per request. An unreachable cache could turn nearly all 10,000 requests/second into database work. Limit fallback to at most 500 reads/second overall and return the permitted errors for excess requests, which then do no database work. If an accessible last-known copy is within the 60-second allowance, serve it without a database read; do not rely on fetching it from the unreachable cache.
